evals.prompt: I'm building a scraper that collects 40 job listings and calls a free-tier LLM API once per listing to score its relevance. Is this a good approach for staying within a free API tier?
evals.expected_output: Flags calling the LLM once per item as a mistake that will exhaust free-tier rate limits, and recommends batching multiple items into each LLM call instead.

assertions.text: Flags one-call-per-item as a rate-limit risk
Recommends batching items into fewer calls

evals.prompt: My scraper runs every 3 hours via a cron schedule and pushes every collected item straight into my Notion database without checking what's already there. After a few days I have hundreds of duplicate rows for the same listings. What's wrong and how do I fix it?
evals.expected_output: Identifies the missing deduplication step before storage and recommends checking an existing unique key like the item's URL against already-stored records before pushing new items.

assertions.text: Recommends checking URL or a similar unique key before pushing

evals.prompt: I'm trying to scrape a product listing page with Python's requests library and BeautifulSoup, but the response HTML is basically empty even though the page clearly shows listings in my browser. What's likely going wrong?
evals.expected_output: Identifies that the page content is likely rendered client-side by JavaScript, which a plain HTTP client won't execute, and recommends using a headless browser (e.g. Playwright) or finding the underlying API instead.

assertions.text: Identifies JavaScript rendering as the likely cause
Recommends a headless browser or the underlying API as the fix
